title: Leishmania life cycle images in the cutaneous cytologic smear of an immunocompetent patient
case_text:
A 61-year-old immunocompetent Italian man, born and residing in Abruzzo, presented to our observation because of the persistence of multiple ulcerative nodules on the skin of his right cheek (larger nodule measured 2 cm in maximum diameter), partially covered by scaly scabs.
A complete blood picture was normal. The patient referred no travels and had received several topical treatments (antibiotics, antimycotics, steroids), which had failed. After cleaning off the excess blood, cytology smears were performed by sampling cells from the ulcer with a sterile lancet and by smearing the sample directly onto glass slides. Pathological examination showed the presence of a large number of intra- and extracellular Leishmania promastigotes and a massive histiocyte infiltration, laden with amastigotes (Leishman-Donovan bodies) [Figure 1].

   - STRICTLY EXCLUDE from <case_prompt>:
     * Any mention of the disease name or pathogen genus/species (e.g., do not write "Leptospirosis", "Burkholderia", "Leishmania", "Paragonimus").

     * The clinical outcome or treatment response (these belong in the diagnostic reasoning, not the presentation).

3. STRUCTURE OF <diagnostic_reasoning>:
   - Enumerate all alternative candidate diagnoses considered in the text.
   - For each candidate, provide a concise summary explaining why it was considered and why it was ruled out in this patient, followed by a direct verbatim quote from the article in quotation marks.
   - Conclude with the Diagnostic Pivot: the pivotal clinical and confirmatory turning point that established the confirmed diagnosis.

4. TARGET CANONICAL DISEASE:
   - The verified ground-truth disease for this patient is: Leishmaniasis
   - Disease subtype / specific manifestation: cutaneous leishmaniasis
